title: Pronouns
note: Say the pronoun, then the word: no “is / am / are” needed. For هِيَّ (she), add ـة (-a) to the describing word.

rows.gulf: إِحْنَا is spoken Gulf; the slide also gives نَحْنُ (formal).

title: Possessive endings (my, your, his…)
note: Stick the ending on the end of the noun. A word ending in ـة changes to ـت before the ending: سَيَّارَة → سَيَّارْتِي (my car).

rows.gulf: Gulf speech says -ah (اِسْمَهْ); the slide writes it -hu (Ismhu).
ـچ (-ich) is the Gulf way; the slide gives both Kithabik and Kithabich.

title: Past tense: he drank, I drank…
note: He = the plain verb (شَرَبْ). Add the ending for the others: they -oo, she -at, you / I -t, you all -too, you (f) -ti, we -na.

rows.gulf: إِحْنَا is spoken Gulf; the slide writes نَحْنُ (Nahn).

title: Past tense practice: opened, sat, accepted
note: The slide's practice verbs with the answer key. Same endings as شَرَبْ.

title: Present tense: he drinks, I drink…
note: Remember NATY: put ن (N, we), أ (A, I), ت (T, you / she) or ي (Y, he / they) in front of the verb. You all and they add -oon, you (f) adds -een.

title: Present tense practice: opens, sits, accepts
note: The slide's practice verbs with the answer key.

title: Future tense: he will drink…
note: بـ (bi) + the present verb. For أَنَا drop the أ and add بـ straight on: أَشْرَبْ → بَشْرَبْ (Ana bashrab).

title: Past · present · future side by side
note: All with هُوَّ (he). Present = NATY + past; future = بـ + present.

rows.gulf: In the UAE you'll also hear سَارْ / يِسِيرْ for “go” (Day 10 and Day 13).

title: Past continuous: he was drinking…
note: كَانْ (was) + the present verb. كَانْ changes with the person, the verb keeps its present form.

title: Everyday phrases: work, going, asking
from: Picked from your lessons (day shown on each row)

rows.ar: رِحْتْ إِلَى السُّوقْ وَبَعْدَيْنْ سِرْتْ إِلَى الدَّوَامْ
rows.t: Riht ilas-soog wa ba'dain sirt ilad-dawam
rows.en: I went to the market and then went to work
rows.ta: நான் சந்தைக்குப் போய்விட்டு பின் வேலைக்குச் சென்றேன்

rows.en: I have to go to work after an hour
rows.ta: ஒரு மணி நேரம் கழித்து நான் வேலைக்கு செல்ல வேண்டும்

rows.en: Walk straight and take a right
Not later, I want it now
Can you give me your number?
rows.ta: தயவுசெய்து உங்களது நம்பரை எனக்கு தர முடியுமா?

rows.en: I want to buy a mobile from Lulu
rows.ta: நான் லூலூவில் இருந்து மொபைல் வாங்க விரும்புகிறேன்

title: Numbers 0–20
note: 3 to 10 take a plural noun: عِنْدِي أَرْبَعَة كُتُبْ (I have 4 books). 11 and up take a singular noun: تِسْعْطَعَشْ قَلَمْ (19 pens).

title: Tens, hundreds, thousands
note: 21–99: say the ones first, then وْ (and), then the tens: 36 = سِتَّة وْثَلَاثِينْ (six and thirty). Over 100, join every part with وْ: 151 = مِيَّة وْوَاحِدْ وْخَمْسِينْ.

title: First, second, third…
note: Use the feminine form with a feminine word: الْغُرْفَة الْخَامْسَة (the 5th room), الصَّفّْ السَّابِعْ (the 7th class).

title: Days of the week
note: Put يُومْ (day) in front: عِنْدَنَا اجْتِمَاعْ يُومِ السَّبْتْ (We have a meeting on Saturday).

title: Time words
note: Gulf words come first; the second word in a pair is the one the slide also gives.

title: The hours (what time is it?)
note: Spoken Gulf just says السَّاعَة + the number. The slide uses the formal feminine ordinal (السَّاعَة الْوَاحِدَة).

title: Minutes: past & to
note: وْ (and) = past the hour. إِلَّا (except) = to the next hour.

title: “How are you?” around the Gulf
note: Any of these works in the UAE. Answer with الْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهْ، زِينْ or أَنَا بِخَيْرْ.

title: Man, woman, group: same phrase, three endings
note: Talking to a woman usually adds -een / -i; talking to a group adds -oon / -u.

title: Direction words
note: Pairs: the first word is the Gulf one you'll hear most.

rows.gulf: لِينْ is spoken Gulf; the slide uses حَتَّى.

title: One, two, many (broken plurals)
note: Two of anything: add ـيْنْ (-ain). Many: the word changes shape, so learn each plural with its word. Remember: numbers 3–10 use the plural (ثَلَاثَة كُتُبْ).
